title: Unify the handling of installing and updating processes
description: Our handling of installing requirements are pretty inconsistent. We have the Titanium SDK Updater which checks on startup for updates to Titanium SDK, titanium CLI, alloy, and acs. But we also have separate IStartup checks for acs and alloy. Additionally our check for Node is done entirely separately.    Ideally we'd have the check for updates _always_ run regardless of prefs. And we should have the notion of required installs versus optional (so user can ignore updates that aren't required, but must install/update required things).

title: Provide Content Assist for attribute names in Alloy view XML files
description: Alloy uses XML files to define views. We should provide content assist for the attributes of elements.      For attribute CA we need to look up the properties for the given element's type in the JS index, as well as the events.    To look up the type name, we take the element name as the type name and determine the namespace prefix. The default prefix is {{Titanium.UI.}}. If there is an {{ns}} attribute, use it's value as the namespace. Alloy will provide us with the exceptions to the rule for namespace mappings.    e.g.  {{View}} -> {{Titanium.UI.View}}  {{Label}} -> {{Titanium.UI.Label}}  {{<View ns=""""Ti.Map""""/>}} -> {{Titanium.Map.View}}  {{Toolbar}} -> {{Titanium.UI.iOS.Toolbar}}    The list of attribute name proposals is:  # The list of properties of the type  # The list of events of the type. Each event name is transformed to be {{""""on"""" + Character.toUppercase(event.name().charAt(0)) + event.name().substring(1);}} - i.e. """"click"""" -> """"onClick""""  # The common set of attributes: {{class}}, {{id}} and {{ns}}.    It should be noted that the {{Alloy}} element may only have {{class}} and {{id}} attributes. The special {{Require}} element may have {{class}}, {{id}}, {{src}}, and {{type}}.

title: Allow users to package multiple module projects as one zip
description: Currently Studio only allows packaging of single module projects. title: Index external build path entries separately from project index
description: Our current mechanism for build path entries is not as flexible and useful as we'll need to properly make use of it for NodeJs/Titanium/etc.  Currently we can only have a contributor that supplies entries pointing at single files (JSCA), and hook them up to projects. The list is stored as a persistent property ont he project - which is not portable across workspaces and other users, so we should likely write them out to a {{.buildpath}} file likes JDT does with {{.classpath}}.     Additionally, those files are """"contributed"""" to the list run through our builder for a project. So they get merged into the project's index itself. For each build entry we should be able to point at a single file or a directory tree, and then index all of it. Each entry should be recorded into it's own index file, so multiple projects referencing the same entry can reuse the same index (i.e. Titanium SDK 2.1.4GA API).    Lastly, the querying of indices would need to be altered os that we can ask for the ordered list of entries for a project, get the corresponding indices and query them. (rather than hard-coding the project's index and sometimes the """"metadata"""" index).

description: If the debug on iOS device session is terminated in Studio, then it does not close the app running on device. title: Store build path entries in a format that can be shared across users and checked into SCM
description: We currently store build paths as a persistent property on the project. This is done by Eclipse and causes some issues, namely:  - This cannot be shared with another user since it's stored outside the project. Other developers on the project won't have the same buildpath when they grab a copy of the project (typically through SCM).  - Eclipse has a limit on the size of the data it can hold this way. It says it holds ~2Kb strings, which could become an issue for projects with many build paths.

title: Retain ordering of build path entries

This would also involve updating the build path entry UI to use an ordered list, allowing users to move entries up and down in the list.

We should either have the method accept a force parameter to not use the cache if there are different cases to distinguish or always not to cache.
